# T6 counterexample-guided refinement of R1

Rule: `vm_pu.11 < tau`. Each iteration: search oracle (Stage A, 10000 cached LHS samples; Stage B, DE with 2000 power flows) and exact oracle (Z3, LinDistFlow). tau moves 0.0001 pu below the lowest counterexample voltage (AC value for search, LinDistFlow value for exact). Stop at no counterexample in both layers, or after 10 iterations.

| 1 | 0.94281 | 358 | 542 | SAT | 16 | search-A 0.91761; search-B 0.90827; exact 0.93590 | tau -> 0.90817 | 5.7 |
| 2 | 0.90817 | 0 | 1 | SAT | 4 | search-B 0.90672; exact 0.90000 | tau -> 0.89990 | 4.7 |
| 3 | 0.89990 | 0 | 0 | UNSAT | 0 | ⟨none⟩ | stop: no counterexample in either layer | 2.7 |

Reading: the firing band is measured inside the voltages the envelope calls benign. If the final tau is at or below 0.90 pu, the refined rule fires only on states that already violate the operating limit. A voltage limit alarm already catches those, so as an intrusion rule it is useless.
